title: Soft Body Sculptor Robot Workshop
description: A robot artist stands beside a ShaderBall that behaves as a soft, deformable body. The user clicks and drags on the ShaderBall surface to create deformation dents, adjusts softness and damping parameters via sliders, and commands the robot to poke, squeeze, or restore the ball through a control panel. The robot animates toward the ball and triggers procedural soft body deformations.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a soft body sculptor workshop. Load ShaderBall.glb centered at origin and robot.glb positioned at (3, 0, 0) facing the ball. Use GLTFLoader from three/addons. Setup: PerspectiveCamera at (0, 3, 8) with OrbitControls, ambient light intensity 0.6, directional light at (5, 10, 5) with shadows enabled, and a ground plane with receiveShadow. Soft Body System: Represent the ShaderBall mesh vertices as a soft body by storing original vertex positions. On mouse click-and-drag (raycaster intersection with the ball), displace nearby vertices inward along their normals using a Gaussian falloff kernel. Maintain a velocity buffer per vertex that applies spring-back force toward rest positions, scaled by a damping parameter. Each frame, integrate velocities and update geometry with computeVertexNormals(). Provide three dat.gui or HTML sliders: softness (0.1-1.0, controls displacement magnitude), damping (0.01-0.5, controls spring recovery speed), and radius (0.1-1.5, controls deformation brush size). Robot Interactions: Add an HTML panel with buttons: Poke, Squeeze, Restore. When Poke is clicked, animate the robot sliding toward the ball over 1 second using TWEEN or manual lerp, then trigger a single-point deformation at a random surface point, then slide back. Squeeze triggers symmetric deformations on opposite sides simultaneously. Restore gradually resets all vertices to original positions over 2 seconds with eased interpolation. Validate that softness, damping, and radius parameters are within their defined ranges before applying any deformation. Display a vertex displacement heatmap by coloring vertices from blue (no displacement) to red (max displacement) using a custom vertex-color shader or BufferAttribute colors. Show a live stats counter of total displaced vertices and maximum displacement magnitude. The robot should have a subtle idle bobbing animation when not performing actions.
